reference_title: UFC 3-301-01, Structural Engineering (DoD, dated 11 April 2023, as amended through Change 4, 3 June 2025)
chapter_title: Modifications to ASCE 7-16 for Critical Healthcare Facilities

sections.title: ASCE 7-16 Chapter 11 - Seismic Design Criteria
sections.summary: Adopts modifications from 2022 CBC Section 1617A to ASCE 7-16, applying IN ADDITION to Chapter 3 for the same SDC D/E/F healthcare facilities defined in Chapter 6, governing on conflict.
sections.body: This Chapter adopts some of the modifications made by Section 1617A of the 2022 California Building Code to ASCE 7-16 for DoD's critical healthcare facilities, cited against the 2021 IBC / ASCE 7-16 / ACI 318-19 / TMS 402-16 / AISC 360-16 / AISC 341-16 basis (the 2025-CBC/2024-IBC edition was not yet available). 11.1.2 [Supplement]: for the SDC D/E/F facilities of Chapter 6 (Group I-2 Condition 2, emergency-surgery ambulatory care), this chapter's modifications apply IN ADDITION to Chapter 3; this chapter governs on conflict.
key_points: Same edition basis and facility scope as Chapter 6 (2021 IBC / ASCE 7-16 family)
Applies in addition to Chapter 3, governing on conflict, for SDC D/E/F healthcare facilities
sections.applicability: Same scope as Chapter 6: SDC D/E/F Group I-2 Condition 2 and emergency-surgery ambulatory care facilities.

sections.title: ASCE 7-16 Chapter 12 - Seismic Design Requirements for Building Structures
sections.summary: Adds structural-configuration limits (uniform bay spacing, transfer-beam restriction, 125%-sized seismic joints, 2 in./story separation), lightweight-concrete and steel-eccentrically-braced-frame limitations, Table 7-1 (a curated permitted-systems-only subset of Table 3-1), vertical-combination R/Cd/Omega0 continuity rules, two-stage-analysis-procedure modifications, prohibited horizontal/vertical irregularities, a lateral-force addition for grade-differential-supporting buildings, and a structural-separation equation replacement.
sections.body: 12.1.7 [Addition]: structural configuration limits -- essentially uniform bay spacing; transfer beams/trusses supporting upper columns not used unless AHJ-approved case-by-case; seismic joints avoided where possible, else identified at schematic design and AHJ-approved, sized for >=125% of the ASCE 7-16 required separation (accounting for story drift, diaphragm displacement/rotation, and ultimate-limit-state stiffness for concrete); non-integral adjacent structures separated by >=2 in./story. 12.1.8 [Addition]: lightweight concrete NOT permitted in seismic-force-resisting members, except floor/roof diaphragm slabs. 12.1.9 [Addition]: steel eccentrically braced systems must keep nonstructural-component connections (precast panels, elevator guide rails, staircase supports, pipe supports, etc.) away from EBF link beams. 12.2.1 [Supplement]: Table 7-1 of this UFC replaces ASCE 7-16 Table 12.2-1 for healthcare facilities -- ONLY the systems in Table 7-1 are permitted within this chapter's scope; other ASCE 7-16-permitted SDC D/E/F systems (including seismic isolation/damping) require written AHJ approval demonstrating equivalent performance (initial/maintenance cost, nonstructural-component bracing requirements, economic-loss/disruption risk, other benefits). 12.2.3.1 [Replacement]: for vertical combinations, R at any story <= the lowest R used at any story above; Cd and Omega0 at any story >= the largest values used above. 12.2.3.2 [Supplement]: two-stage analysis modifications -- lower-portion stiffness >=10x upper-portion stiffness (base shear vertically distributed per Section 12.8, stiffness = story base shear / elastic displacement with the portion fixed at its base, lower portion includes amplified upper-portion reactions); Horizontal/Vertical Irregularity Type 4 at the portion transition amplifies upper-portion reactions per Sections 12.3.3.3/12.10.1.1/12.10.3.3; overstrength-governed upper-portion member design amplifies loads considered in lower-portion design. 12.3.3.1 [Replacement]: Horizontal Irregularity Type 1b (Table 12.3-1) and Vertical Irregularity Types 1b/5a/5b (Table 12.3-2) are PROHIBITED for SDC D-F. 12.7.3 [Addition]: buildings laterally supporting earth-retaining walls with >6 ft exterior-grade differential on opposite sides add the geotechnically-determined seismic earth-pressure increment (higher side) plus the earth-pressure differential to design lateral forces; existing 12.7.3/12.7.4 renumbered 12.7.4/12.7.5. 12.12.3 [Replacement]: replaces ASCE 7-16 Eq 12.12-1 with delta_M = Cd*delta_max (see ``seismic_load_combinations.structural_separation_healthcare``).
key_points: Table 7-1 is a curated PERMITTED-ONLY subset of Table 3-1 for healthcare facilities -- other systems need written AHJ approval with a documented equivalence case
Seismic joints must be sized at >=125% of the ASCE 7-16 requirement
Lightweight concrete prohibited in seismic-force-resisting members (diaphragm slabs excepted)
Two of the four ASCE 7-16 Table 12.3-1/12.3-2 irregularity types are prohibited outright for SDC D-F
Buildings retaining >6 ft of differential grade must add a geotechnically-determined seismic earth-pressure increment to design forces
sections.applicability: Structural system selection and configuration for critical healthcare facilities; the earth-pressure addition specifically for buildings retaining differential grade.

sections.title: ASCE 7-16 Chapter 13 - Seismic Design Requirements for Nonstructural Components
sections.summary: Accepts HCAI OSP-preapproved equipment as satisfying ASCE 7-16 Special Seismic Certification; sets prequalification-standard requirements (and screw-anchor restrictions) for post-installed anchors/inserts; requires special access floors (with exceptions) and elevator-guide-rail design criteria including a 0.5g minimum ASD seismic force.
sections.body: 13.2.2 [Supplement]: Special Seismic Certification per ASCE 7-16 Section 13.2.2 is deemed satisfied for equipment/components on HCAI's Special Seismic Certification Preapproval (OSP) list (PIN 55; basis is ICC-ES AC156 shake-table testing). 13.4.2.3 [Replacement]: post-installed anchors/specialty inserts in concrete need prequalification per ACI 355.2, ACI 355.4, ICC-ES AC193/AC232/AC308/AC446; masonry anchors need ICC-ES AC01/AC58/AC106; screw anchors limited to dry interior conditions, not permitted in exterior envelopes, and re-use of screw anchors/holes is not permitted. 13.5.7 [Supplement]: all access floors at hospitals/correctional treatment centers must be Special Access Floors (Section 13.5.7.2), except raised-roof/exterior-floor paver systems. 13.6.11.1.1 [Addition]: elevator guide-rail support-bracket fastenings/framing designed for counterweight or car weight plus >=40% rated load; seismic forces distributed 1/3 to top guiding members, 2/3 to bottom; minimum ASD-level seismic force of 0.5g in any horizontal direction (in addition to ASCE 7-16 Section 13.6.11.1) -- see ``healthcare_modifications.healthcare_elevator_seismic_force_asd``.
key_points: HCAI OSP-preapproved equipment satisfies ASCE 7-16 Special Seismic Certification automatically

Post-installed anchor prequalification standards are more extensive than the general Chapter 3 list (adds ICC-ES AC193/AC232/AC308/AC446/AC01/AC58/AC106); screw anchors restricted to dry interior use, no re-use
Elevator guide rails: minimum 0.5g ASD seismic force, 1/3-top / 2/3-bottom load distribution, 40% rated-load counterweight allowance
sections.applicability: Nonstructural component certification, anchorage, access floors, and elevator design at critical healthcare facilities.

sections.title: ASCE 7-16 Chapter 17 - Seismic Design Requirements for Seismically Isolated Structures
sections.summary: Linear analysis procedures are prohibited for seismically isolated structures in Seismic Design Category E or F.
sections.body: 17.4.2.3 [Addition]: linear procedures must NOT be used for seismically isolated structures assigned to SDC E or F.
key_points: SDC E/F seismically isolated structures require nonlinear analysis procedures
sections.applicability: Seismically isolated critical healthcare facilities in SDC E or F.

sections.title: ASCE 7-16 Chapter 18 - Seismic Design Requirements for Structures with Damping Systems
sections.summary: For the nonlinear response history procedure exception, MCER response is based on the single largest-response ground motion, not an averaged suite response.
sections.body: 18.3 [Supplement]: add to the Exception -- for this section, MCER response is based on the largest response from a single ground motion, not the average response of a suite of ground motions.
key_points: MCER response for this exception uses the single worst-case ground motion, not a suite average
sections.applicability: Damped structures using the ASCE 7-16 Section 18.3 nonlinear response history procedure exception.
